title: Normalized descent of common-stage fibre transport
statement: Let k be a field, l a prime invertible in k, R a continuous rational realization family, and Ω an algebraic closure of Q_l. Fix normalized finite fibres ω, normalized pullback comparisons α and normalized scalar comparisons β as in [lem-per-adic-normalized-fibre-pullback, lem-per-adic-normalized-fibre-scalar]. Suppose CommonStageHeartExactness [def-per-common-stage-fibre-descent-interfaces] is supplied. Then CommonStageFibreTransport for these same ω,α,β is inhabited. Its common-point functors are exact, additive and finite dimensional, with their natural finite-stage comparison. Its scalar and actual pullback comparisons retain the prescribed β, tensor associator, underlying transIso and α normalizations, and their identity and composition laws. No joint detection assertion is included.

proof.text:
For a finite heart pair put $V_{\bar x}(E,F)=\omega_{\bar x,E}(F)\otimes_E\Omega$. The finite functor is additive and finite dimensional by [lem-per-adic-normalized-fibre-exactness]. For $M\supset E$, let $b_{M/E,F}$ be $\beta_{M/E,F}$ tensored with $\Omega$ followed by $(W\otimes_E M)\otimes_M\Omega\cong W\otimes_E\Omega$. Set
$$V_{\bar x}[M,u]=b_{M/L,G}(\omega_{\bar x,M}(u)\otimes_M1)b_{M/E,F}^{-1}.$$
For $N\supset M$, put $A_H=\omega_{\bar x,N}(a_{N,M,E,H})\otimes_N1$ for an object $H$ at stage $E$. The coefficient-composition equation of [lem-per-adic-normalized-fibre-scalar] says $b_{N/E,H}A_H=b_{M/E,H}b_{N/M,T_{M/E}H}$, with the canonical tensor identifications understood. Substitute $u_N=a_{N,M,L,G}T_{N/M}(u)a_{N,M,E,F}^{-1}$ from [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category]. Naturality of $\beta_{N/M}$ cancels the two inner $b_{N/M}$ factors, so the displayed prescription for $[N,u_N]$ equals that for $[M,u]$. Equivalent representatives agree after one enlargement by [prop-weil-pbc-common-stage-calculus], hence give equal maps.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14; explicit descent using the normalized scalar cocycle

proof.text: Represent two composable arrows at one stage using [prop-weil-pbc-common-stage-calculus]. In the product of their displayed fibre maps the target comparison of the first is the source comparison of the second, so they cancel; functoriality of $\omega$ gives the map of the composite. The normalized identity $\beta_{E/E}$ gives the identity map. Represent a sum at one stage; additivity of $\omega$ gives its sum. Thus $V$ is an additive functor on heart pairs. For an object $A$ in their isomorphism closure choose $h_A:j_EF\xrightarrow{\sim}A$, put $V(A)=V(E,F)$, and send $f:A\to B$ to $V(h_B^{-1}fh_A)$. Cancellation proves functoriality. A second choice $h'_A$ gives the comparison $V((h'_A)^{-1}h_A)$; these comparisons are natural and satisfy their cocycle equation by composition. Every common heart object has such a presentation by [lem-per-adic-common-stage-truncations].

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14; identities, composition, addition and replete-heart transport

proof.text: At every finite stage, [lem-per-adic-normalized-fibre-exactness] sends a short exact heart sequence to a short exact sequence of finite-dimensional vector spaces. Tensoring that sequence with $\Omega$ stays short exact by [lem-weil-field-scalar-extension-exact]. Present a common short exact sequence by the finite-stage short exact sequence just constructed. Its $V$-sequence is this tensored fibre sequence, conjugated by the prescribed $b$ and presentation isomorphisms, so it too is short exact. Thus every $V_{\bar x}$ is exact. For an arrow $v:A\to B$, apply this exactness to $0\to\ker v\to A\to\operatorname{im}v\to0$ and $0\to\operatorname{im}v\to B\to\operatorname{coker}v\to0$. The resulting injection of the fibre of $\operatorname{im}v$ into that of $B$ and surjection from that of $A$ identify the kernel, image and cokernel of $V(v)$. Applying this to the image-to-kernel quotient also identifies homology.

Use the actual common-stage heart pullback furnished by [lem-per-adic-stratified-pullback-texact]. For a heart pair $(E,F)$ define its fibre comparison at $\bar y$ by $\alpha_{g,F}\otimes_E1$, with $\bar x=g\bar y$. For an arrow $[M,u]$, its actual pullback representative is $g^*u$ conjugated by the actual pullback/scalar comparisons. The mixed $\alpha,\beta$ equation of [lem-per-adic-normalized-fibre-scalar] identifies those conjugations, after taking fibres, with the source and target $b_{M/E}$ and $b_{M/L}$ in the prescription above. Naturality of $\alpha$ from [lem-per-adic-normalized-fibre-pullback] then reads
$$\alpha_{g,G}V_{\bar y}(g^*[M,u])=V_{\bar x}([M,u])\alpha_{g,F},$$
where all maps are extended to $\Omega$. The coefficient-composition equation already used in descent makes this equality independent of further enlargement. On arbitrary heart presentations conjugate by $h_A$ as above; naturality makes the resulting comparison independent of the presentation up to its specified natural isomorphisms. The identity and composite-pullback equations hold on every finite heart pair by the corresponding equations for $\alpha$, and hence on all presentations. For the transition object $T_{L/E}F$ the definition of $b_{L/E,F}$ is exactly $\beta_{L/E,F}$ extended to $\Omega$ followed by the balanced-tensor associator, proving the final normalization.
